- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- Model frequently overpredicts mean reversion in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead); adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.22), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to catch momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates final price; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment is weak or flat over last 5–7 days.
